newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Ginanjar says economy sound.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Ginanjar says economy sound.

text.p: Indonesia's State Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Friday the country's economy was sound as it entered a new era with the float of the rupiah.
He told reporters that Indonesia's balance of payments and foreign exchange reserves were unlikely to be sharply affected by the fall in the rupiah.

"The latest government monetary policy shows that we are really consistent. If they (speculators) see the government will not intervene, we hope they will reduce their speculative activity," Ginanjar said.
"Our fundamental economy is sound. We are entering a new era of market principles. It is the correct time for the government to carry out such a policy," he said.
"Our condition is different from Thailand and the fundementals of the economy are also different," Ginanjar said.
"Our balance of payments are safe as well as foreign exchange reserves," he said.
A structural weakness in Thailand's economy triggered speculative attacks on South East Asian currencies in late june and the malaise has subsequently spread throughout the region.
